title: PC in VLAN 10 Cannot Ping Default Gateway
symptom: Host PC-1 (192.168.10.50/24) cannot reach its default gateway 192.168.10.1 on Router R1. Link light on switch is amber.
topology: PC-1 (Fa0/1) -> Switch SW1 (Gig0/1) -> Router R1 (Gig0/0.10 Subinterface)
show_outputs:
SW1# show vlan brief
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -------------------------------
1    default                          active    Fa0/2, Fa0/3, Fa0/4
10   Engineering                      active    
20   Sales                            active    Fa0/5, Fa0/6

SW1# show running-config interface FastEthernet0/1
interface FastEthernet0/1
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 1
 spanning-tree portfast

PC-1# ipconfig
IP Address: 192.168.10.50
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 192.168.10.1
expected_fault: Switch port Fa0/1 is assigned to VLAN 1 (default) instead of VLAN 10.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Access port FastEthernet0/1 is configured for default VLAN 1, while PC-1 has an IP in subnet 192.168.10.0/24 corresponding to VLAN 10.
ai_diagnosis.evidence_quote: SW1# show running-config interface FastEthernet0/1 -> 'switchport access vlan 1' while PC-1 is on 192.168.10.50.

human_review.notes: Diagnosis is accurate and evidence directly matches the show run output. Approved fix.

title: Subnet Mask Mismatch Preventing Gateway Ping
symptom: Host PC-3 (10.0.1.130) cannot ping default gateway 10.0.1.1 on Router R2. Neighbor PC-4 (10.0.1.50) has no issues.
show_outputs:
PC-3# ipconfig
IP Address: 10.0.1.130
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.128
Default Gateway: 10.0.1.1

R2# show ip interface brief | include GigabitEthernet0/1
GigabitEthernet0/1     10.0.1.1        YES manual up                    up

R2# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/1
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip address 10.0.1.1 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: PC-3 is configured with a /25 mask (255.255.255.128). IP 10.0.1.130 falls in range 10.0.1.128-10.0.1.255, making gateway 10.0.1.1 (in 10.0.1.0-10.0.1.127) appear as an off-subnet address requiring an unreachable default gateway.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Subnet mask mismatch on PC-3. With mask 255.255.255.128 (/25), host 10.0.1.130 resides in subnet 10.0.1.128/25, so it considers gateway 10.0.1.1 outside its local broadcast domain.
ai_diagnosis.evidence_quote: PC-3# Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.128 vs R2 interface Gig0/1: ip address 10.0.1.1 255.255.255.0

human_review.notes: Correct calculation of /25 boundary split. Verified.

title: Extended ACL Blocking Web Traffic Due to Inverted Wildcard Mask
symptom: Branch workstation PC-10 (172.16.10.25) cannot browse internal web server at 10.10.10.80 (HTTP port 80). Router drops packets.
show_outputs:
R1# show access-lists 101
Extended IP access list 101
    10 permit tcp 172.16.10.0 255.255.255.0 host 10.10.10.80 eq www (0 matches)
    20 deny ip any any (142 matches)

R1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/1
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip address 172.16.10.1 255.255.255.0
 ip access-group 101 in
expected_fault: ACL 101 line 10 used a subnet mask (255.255.255.0) instead of an inverted wildcard mask (0.0.0.255). Cisco IOS interprets 255.255.255.0 as wildcard 255.255.255.0, resulting in 0 matches and hitting deny any any.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: The access-list 101 statement uses normal subnet mask notation 255.255.255.0 rather than wildcard mask 0.0.0.255. This causes the rule to fail matching source traffic, defaulting to implicit deny line 20.
ai_diagnosis.evidence_quote: R1# show access-lists 101 -> '10 permit tcp 172.16.10.0 255.255.255.0 host 10.10.10.80 eq www (0 matches)' and '20 deny ip any any (142 matches)'

human_review.notes: AI identified wildcard mask error correctly, but also forgot that DNS (UDP 53) and HTTPS (TCP 443) may be needed. Added permit for port 443 and domain.

Gi0/1       on               802.1q         trunking      99

Port        Mode             Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gi0/1       on               802.1q         trunking      1
expected_fault: Native VLAN mismatch across 802.1Q trunk: Switch-1 uses Native VLAN 99, while Switch-2 uses Native VLAN 1.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Native VLAN inconsistency on the trunk link between Switch-1 (VLAN 99) and Switch-2 (VLAN 1), causing STP inconsistencies and potential frame leakage between VLAN 1 and 99.

title: NAT Pool IP Address Conflict with Router Interface

expected_fault: NAT pool PUBLIC_POOL includes 203.0.113.1, which is already assigned to the router's physical interface Gig0/1.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: The dynamic NAT pool starts at 203.0.113.1, colliding with the IP address assigned to router interface GigabitEthernet0/1 (203.0.113.1).
ai_diagnosis.evidence_quote: NAT pool PUBLIC_POOL '203.0.113.1' vs Gig0/1 IP '203.0.113.1'; %IP-4-DUPADDR logged

R-NAT(config)# ip nat pool PUBLIC_POOL 203.0.113.2 203.0.113.6 netmask 255.255.255.248

human_review.notes: Fix excludes router interface IP from pool. Alternatively 'ip nat inside source list 1 interface Gi0/1 overload' can be used.
